newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - Aug 5.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - Aug 5.

text.p: These are the leading stories in Manila newspapers on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Defense Secretary Renato de Villa said yesterday he submitted his resignation to President Ramos last July 20 to concentrate on his plans to seek the presidency in the 1998 elections. He also expressed his willingness to face the Senate inquiry on his alleged misappropriation of calamity funds. (STAR/TODAY)

- As Congress readied an investigation into the latest round of oil price increases yesterday, government workers renewed their demand for new wage increases and militant labour groups mobilised their forces for a nationwide transport strike on Friday. (STANDARD)

- A nine-man Senate panel, the National Bureau of Investigation and the Philippine National Police Narcotics Command initially cleared four sentaors of alleged involvement in illegal drug trade. (BULLETIN)

- The government needs to contain the inflation rate at an average of eight percent in the second half of the year to meet its six percent to 6.5 percent target for 1997, Planning Secretary Cielito Habito said in an interview. (BUSINESSWORLD)

- Business leader Raul Concepcion, president of the Federation of Philippine Industries, yesterday warned of an impending economic recession if the central bank is unable to stop the peso from falling and interest rates from rising. (ALL NEWSPAPERS)

- The government sees the country's trade deficit this year to narrow to $12.54 billion from the earlier $13.85 billion projected under the economic programme with the International Monetary Fund. (TODAY/STAR/CHRONICLE)
